## Summary

Fixed both real gaps found in round 4 of the interactive-session write gate, on PR #80's branch (`worker/task-20260726-083833-build-interactive-session-write-gate--re`, commit `353fa09`):

1. **Argv-position bypass (fixed):** Both `git` and `gh` wrappers previously checked only `argv[1]` literally. Rewrote detection to scan the full argv and skip real, version-confirmed global flags (`git -C`, `--git-dir`, `-c`, etc.; `gh -R`/`--repo` in all 4 real forms) before finding the subcommand. Verified live: `git -C /tmp push origin master`, `git --git-dir=/tmp/.git push origin master`, and `gh --repo some/repo pr merge 1 --merge` are all now blocked.

2. **systemd-run impersonation (investigated honestly, mitigated):** Live-tested `systemd-run --user --unit=veridian-worker@<fake>.service --scope` on VERIDIAN-DEV — it's currently rejected by systemd itself (collides with the real installed template unit files), confirmed this isn't systemd-run being broken in general. But since that's a deployment-specific side effect, not a fundamental guarantee, I didn't rely on it. Instead added a third signal: the cgroup-derived task_id must now cross-reference a real, `in_progress` `task.yaml` under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/`, closing the gap regardless of how a matching-but-fake cgroup name might be produced.

Extended `tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh` (65/65 scenarios pass) and added `tests/write_gate_test.py` so `python3 -m pytest tests/ -k write_gate -v` exits 0. Updated the guard's KNOWN LIMITATIONS and `PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml` A15 article honestly, disclosing the finite/version-tied nature of the new flag allowlist and that the systemd-run collision is incidental, not the actual fix.

Per the task's constraints, this was not merged — it needs a fresh audit pass with live reproduction of the argv-bypass and systemd-run scenarios, not review of the diff alone.
